holidays.name: World Kindness Day
holidays.description: A global day dedicated to doing good deeds, from paying for a stranger's coffee to complimenting a coworker. It is celebrated in many countries, with the goal of showing that small acts of kindness can ripple outward.
holidays.origin: Established in 1998 by the World Kindness Movement, a coalition of kindness organizations that met in Tokyo in 1997. It is observed in countries such as Canada, Japan, Australia, Nigeria, and the United Arab Emirates.
holidays.funFact: The World Kindness Movement began with a 1997 Tokyo conference, and it was not created as a Hallmark-style holiday. Several countries have since adopted the day officially, and the UAE even runs a national Year of Giving.

holidays.name: National Indian Pudding Day
holidays.description: A celebration of Indian pudding, a warm, spiced New England dessert made from cornmeal, milk, molasses, and spices, and often served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream. It is comfort food at its most old-fashioned.
holidays.origin: The dessert dates back to colonial America, where English settlers adapted their hasty pudding recipe using native cornmeal, which they called 'Indian meal.' The food-holiday calendar later adopted November 13 as its day.
holidays.funFact: The 'Indian' in the name has nothing to do with the country or with a particular tribe. It comes from the colonial term for cornmeal, and the pudding is slow-baked for hours until it becomes custardy.

holidays.name: National Sadie Hawkins Day
holidays.description: A day inspired by the comic strip tradition in which women get to chase down and propose to the men of their choice, with the men required to go along. It has inspired many school dances where the roles are flipped.
holidays.origin: Created by cartoonist Al Capp for his comic strip Li'l Abner in 1937. The fictional Sadie Hawkins was 'the homeliest gal in all them hills,' and her father organized a footrace to get her a husband. The strip's holiday was set for November, and its date has varied over the years.
holidays.funFact: Within just a few years of the comic's debut, the day had become so popular that hundreds of colleges were holding Sadie Hawkins events, and Life magazine reported on the craze in 1939.

holidays.name: World Hello Day
holidays.description: A day when people are encouraged to greet at least ten people, with the goal of promoting peace through communication. It is as simple as saying hello to ten strangers, neighbors, or coworkers.
holidays.origin: Started in 1973 in response to the conflict between Egypt and Israel, by brothers Brian and Michael McCormack. They sent letters to world leaders, and the idea has since spread to more than 180 countries.
holidays.funFact: Hello Day began as a reaction to a war, and the founders believed personal communication was more powerful than force. Today people mark it with everything from handshakes to greetings in different languages.

holidays.name: Fish and Chips Day
holidays.description: A salute to the classic British takeaway of battered fried fish with thick-cut chips, ideally doused in vinegar and eaten from paper on a chilly day.
holidays.origin: Fish and chips took off in 19th-century England, with the first shops opening in the 1860s in London and northern England. The unofficial day is a modern food-lovers' observance.
holidays.funFact: Fish and chips were never rationed in Britain during World War II, because the government considered them vital to morale. Winston Churchill reportedly referred to them as 'the good companions.'
